concepts.title: Meaning and Nature of a Debenture
concepts.definition: A debenture is a formal loan certificate issued under the company's seal: it promises interest at a stated rate on fixed dates and repayment of principal after the agreed period, and under section 2(30) it also covers bonds and debenture stock.
concepts.key_idea: The debentureholder is a creditor of the company, not an owner, so interest is owed even in loss years.

solution_steps.explain: a written acknowledgement of debt issued under the common seal, with the rate of interest usually part of its name
interest at a fixed percentage, normally half-yearly, plus principal back after the stated period or in intervals
creditor position: steady charge on profit, priority over shareholders on winding up, no vote in management

concepts.title: Shares versus Debentures
concepts.definition: A share is a slice of the company's owned capital carrying membership rights, while a debenture is borrowed money on paper: the shareholder gets variable dividend and votes, the debentureholder gets fixed interest and no vote, and repayment rules differ sharply on winding up.
concepts.key_idea: Owner money stays with the business; loan money must return on the due date whatever the profits did.
question_patterns: give the points on which shares and debentures differ

solution_steps.explain: share is part of owned capital, debenture is part of borrowed capital
dividend floats with profit and shareholders vote; interest is a fixed charge and debentureholders do not vote
shares are returned last and only on winding up, debentures fall due on the redemption date and rank ahead of shareholders

concepts.title: Types of Debentures
concepts.definition: Debentures sort along four lines: whether a charge backs them (secured or naked), whose name they carry (registered or bearer), whether they ever fall due (redeemable or perpetual), and whether they can change form (convertible into shares or permanently debentures).
concepts.key_idea: Collateral is the anchor question: a mortgage or charge makes the issue safe for the lender even if the business fails.

solution_steps.explain: fixed or floating charge on assets gives secured or mortgage debentures; without charge they are unsecured or naked
registered debentures move through the company's register; bearer debentures are negotiable by delivery
redeemable debentures carry a repayment date, irredeemable ones do not; convertible debentures may turn into shares or new debentures on stated terms

concepts.title: Issue of Debentures at Par, Premium and Discount
concepts.definition: Debenture entries mirror share entries: money received through application and allotment builds up to the debentures account, any issue price above face value credits securities premium reserve, and any shortfall below face value is debited to discount on issue of debentures as a capital loss.
concepts.key_idea: Premium is not income and discount is not expense on day one -- both wait as capital items until written off or settled at redemption.

solution_steps.explain: bank is debited and the debenture application and allotment account credited, then transferred to the debentures account
when issue price exceeds face value, the excess is credited to securities premium reserve
when issue price is below face value, the shortfall is debited to discount on issue of debentures, a capital loss awaiting write-off

concepts.title: Debentures Issued for Consideration other than Cash
concepts.definition: When a company buys assets or a whole business from a vendor and pays with its own debentures, the count of debentures to hand over is the purchase consideration divided by the price at which each debenture is issued.
concepts.key_idea: Assets and liabilities come in at value, the vendor is credited, and settlement runs through the debentures account at par, premium or discount.
question_patterns: how many debentures must be issued to a vendor against purchase consideration

solution_steps.explain: apply the discount or premium to the face value per debenture

solution_steps.explain: purchase consideration owed to the vendor split by the issue price gives the debenture count (rounded to whole debentures, cash for the fraction)

concepts.title: Debentures as Collateral Security
concepts.definition: A company borrowing from a bank may hand over its own debentures as a secondary safeguard on top of the primary security; ownership stays with the company and the bank holds them only until the loan is repaid.
concepts.key_idea: No interest runs on collateral debentures and the books either stay silent or note them through a debentures suspense account.

solution_steps.explain: bank is debited and bank loan credited; the pledge adds nothing to the liability amount
either no entry with a footnote, or debentures suspense debited and debentures credited, and the suspense charge shown contra in the balance sheet
when the loan is settled the entry is cancelled and the debentures come back into the company's own hands

concepts.title: Loss on Issue of Debentures
concepts.definition: Debentures issued below face value but promised back above it create a two-sided loss: the issue discount plus the redemption premium, both booked at once by debiting loss on issue of debentures and crediting premium on redemption of debentures.
concepts.key_idea: Premium on redemption is a liability the company owes later, so it is recognised today, not on the repayment date.
question_patterns: compute the loss on issue of debentures issued at discount and redeemable at premium

solution_steps.explain: face value minus issue price gives the discount per debenture

multiply the per-debenture loss by the number of debentures issued

concepts.title: Interest on Debentures with Tax Deducted at Source
concepts.definition: Debenture interest runs on the nominal value at the stated rate for the elapsed months, is a charge against profit whatever the result, and any tax deducted at source is withheld from the holder and deposited with the government.
concepts.formula: net_interest_paid = debentures_issued * face_value_per_debenture * interest_rate * months / 12 - tax_deduction
concepts.key_idea: The company deducts TDS first, so the holder receives interest net of tax and can claim the credit in its own return.

concepts.title: Writing off Discount or Loss on Issue
concepts.definition: The discount or loss on a debenture issue is a capital loss cleared immediately in the issue year: first to the extent of the securities premium balance, and whatever remains against the statement of profit and loss.
concepts.key_idea: Securities premium soaks up the loss first by law; only the leftover touches revenue profit.

solution_steps.explain: issue discount plus redemption premium per debenture, times the number of debentures

solution_steps.action: charge the residue to revenue profit
solution_steps.explain: whatever the premium could not cover is debited to the statement of profit and loss in the issue year

concepts.title: Redemption Reserve and Investment Rules
concepts.definition: Covered unlisted companies must build a debenture redemption reserve of ten percent of debentures still outstanding, and every company must invest or deposit at least fifteen percent of the debentures maturing during the coming year by the end of April; several classes such as banking companies and NBFCs are exempt.
concepts.key_idea: The reserve comes from profit for the covered classes, the investment is a locked deposit that only redemption may touch.
question_patterns: how much must be invested for redemption of debentures maturing next year

solution_steps.explain: other unlisted companies transfer ten percent of outstanding debentures from surplus to debenture redemption reserve

concepts.title: Redemption in Lump Sum
concepts.definition: On maturity the company pays every debentureholder the redemption price: face value plus any promised premium, with the whole amount settled in one payment on the due date.
concepts.key_idea: Premium on redemption, if any, is paid out of profit or fresh capital and settled together with the principal in one stroke.

concepts.title: Redemption by Conversion into Shares
concepts.definition: Convertible debentures can be redeemed by handing the holder new equity shares: the amount due on the debentures (their actual proceeds where they were issued at discount) is divided by the issue price of the new share to count how many shares to allot.
concepts.key_idea: Only real money raised on the old debentures converts; a discount issue converts at what was actually received, not at face.
question_patterns: how many equity shares are allotted on conversion of debentures

solution_steps.explain: face value of the share plus any premium per share
